title: The Platform That Never Moved
scene: A station volunteer hears an arrival announcement, checks the platform, and shuts the waiting room. No train has arrived, yet she has done exactly the right thing.
explanation: The closed station is a museum. A motion sensor plays the historical arrival recording when the last visitor passes the exit exhibit. The volunteer checks that the platform gallery is empty before closing.
mechanism: An ordinary signal has a different purpose in a changed setting. Distinguish a working railway from a museum.

title: The Greenhouse Umbrella
scene: A gardener opens an umbrella inside a greenhouse every sunny morning. It stays dry, the plants beneath it thrive, and she removes it when the clouds arrive.
explanation: She is comparing shade-tolerant seedlings under filtered and direct light. The umbrella shades one tray during intense sunlight; she removes it when light is already diffuse.
mechanism: A familiar object is used for a different physical property. The weather matters through light rather than rain.

title: The Empty Frame
scene: A curator replaces a celebrated picture with an empty frame for one hour. Visitors who came specifically for that picture thank her afterwards.
explanation: The picture is temporarily resting on a low table for a supervised tactile reproduction workshop. Visitors with limited vision can explore a raised replica mounted behind the removable picture panel. The wall frame is empty while the panel is being used.
mechanism: The observer sees absence at one location but the object has a useful role elsewhere. Ask where it went and who the visitors are.

title: The Backwards Clock
scene: A baker installs a clock whose face looks backwards to everyone at the counter. Her baking becomes more accurate, and she refuses to turn it around.
explanation: She monitors the wall behind her through a mirror above her workbench. A reversed clock face is legible in that mirror, letting her check the time without leaving the dough.
mechanism: The correct viewpoint reverses the apparent anomaly. The design is adapted to the user's indirect line of sight.

title: The Missing Page Numbers
scene: A librarian receives a book with perfectly printed words but apparently missing page numbers. She turns the book upside down, smiles, and accepts it without complaint.
explanation: It is a two-direction reading book: two short works start at opposite covers and meet in the middle. She was examining the second work from the first work's orientation; its page numbers were at the opposite edge.
mechanism: A document has two valid starting points. The observer assumes a conventional layout.

title: The Applause Before the Entrance
scene: An actor receives applause before stepping onstage. The auditorium is empty, and he tells the technician that the timing is finally right.
explanation: He is rehearsing an entrance timed to a recorded applause cue. The technician had previously played the cue too late. Nobody is attending the rehearsal.
mechanism: A social sound can be recorded rather than produced by present observers. Establish whether the event is a performance or rehearsal.

title: The Warm Archive
scene: An archivist leaves a sealed box in a warm room before opening it. Opening it immediately would be faster, but would put the documents at risk.
explanation: The box has just come out of cold storage. Warming it while sealed prevents moist room air from condensing directly on the cold documents when the lid is opened.
mechanism: A delay protects against a change in physical conditions. The risk comes from opening the container, not leaving it closed.

title: The Shorter Route
scene: A courier waits motionless for five minutes at a canal even though an open pedestrian bridge is visible nearby. The wait lets her finish earlier than taking that bridge.
explanation: She is beside a scheduled bicycle ferry that lands directly at her destination. The visible bridge crosses to an island whose only exit requires a long loop, so waiting for the ferry is quicker.
mechanism: Visible distance is not route distance. Compare connected paths rather than apparent proximity.
